nodes.summary: The Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant is the BHH constant of the uniform law on the closed unit square $[0,1]^2$ (Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0,1]^2$): the infimum of the set of real numbers $\beta$ such that i.i.d. samples with this law exist and, for every such sample $X_1, X_2, \dots$, the length of the shortest closed tour through $X_1, \dots, X_n$ divided by $\sqrt{n}$ tends to $\beta$ almost surely.…
nodes.title: Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on the plane and $\beta$ a real number. If, for every real $\gamma$, $\gamma$ is a BHH limit for $\mu$ if and only if $\gamma = \beta$, then the BHH constant of $\mu$ (the infimum of its BHH limits) equals $\beta$.
nodes.title: The BHH constant equals the unique BHH limit

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on the plane, the BHH constant of $\mu$ is the infimum of the set of real numbers $\beta$ that are BHH limits for $\mu$. The infimum of a set of reals that is empty or not bounded below is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: BHH constant of a sampling law

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on the plane, the BHH limit values of $\mu$ form the set of real numbers $\beta$ that are BHH limits for $\mu$.
nodes.title: BHH limit values of a sampling law

nodes.summary: The Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant $\beta_2$ for uniform points in the unit square satisfies $\beta_2 \ge 5/8 = 0.625$.

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that the Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant $\beta_2$ for uniform points in the unit square satisfies $\beta_2 \ge 5/8 = 0.625$, the lower bound reported by Beardwood, Halton and Hammersley (1959).

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a set and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots \colon \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be functions. For an outcome $\omega \in \Omega$ and $n \ge 1$, the normalized tour length is $L_n(\omega)/\sqrt{n}$, where $L_n(\omega)$ is the length of a shortest closed tour through $X_0(\omega), \dots, X_{n-1}(\omega)$. For $n = 0$ it is defined to be $0$.
nodes.title: Normalized tour length

nodes.summary: A planar point is a point of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$: a pair $(x, y)$ of real numbers, with the Euclidean norm $\lVert (x, y) \rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$.

nodes.summary: For points $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ in the Euclidean plane, $L_n$ is the minimum, over all permutations $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the length of the closed tour that visits $x_{\sigma(0)}, \dots, x_{\sigma(n-1)}$ in this order and returns to its start.

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
